messages.author: 5900eadecec2d82d
messages.subject: Re: Trapping web data entry
parts:
Hi Humberto, list,

I've never collected trapping web data, but I can perhaps give some useful
advice about how to put it into Distance.

Each web is equivalent to a single point in a point transect design. The
sample effort is the number of trapping events. Each trapped animal is
equivalent to an observation in a point transect. The distance of the trap
from the centre of the web is the distance to use for this "observation".

So, for example, say I had 1 stratum of area 100, containing 2 webs that I
used for two trapping events (say trap nights). I trapped 3 animals in the
first (at distances 3, 5, 7) and 2 in the second (at distances 4, 5, 8) my
text file for data import might look like this:

area1 100 web1 2 3
area1 100 web1 2 5
area1 100 web1 2 7
area1 100 web1 2 4
area1 100 web1 2 5
area1 100 web1 2 8

Of course 2 webs is not enough to make reliable inferences about the stratum
density, nor is 6 observations enough to reliably fit a detection function,
but you get the idea.

Perhaps others who actually *have* analyzed such data in Distance can send
you some real projects, rather than just advice!

Lots more about trapping webs is in section 6.8 of the Introduction to
Distance Sampling book, and chapter 9 of the Advanced book discusses other
approaches such as trapping line transects. You may also find the trapping
web simulation software WebSim written by Paul Lukacs useful in evaluating
the potential biases in your study
(http://www.cnr.colostate.edu/~plukacs/web.html)
If you get recapture information you may also want to consider using the
free software Density, by Murray Efford
(see http://www.landcareresearch.co.nz/services/software/density/ and
references on that page).

Hope this helps,

- Len
